comments.body:
Thanks for the fix. At f931f6b it looks right: requiring a label or value for paint stops an identifier-only `absoluteFill` view from marking earlier sibling layers as covered, while `semanticShowRect` still treats it as a target. The new test reproduces the tree shape from #4249. There are no conflicts. The repository CI has not run on this head yet, so the unit suite still needs to pass before merge.

Not blocking, take or leave: the test only pins that an identifier-only leaf does not paint, so one more case with an identifier-only leaf in the earlier layer under a higher layer with a hittable full-screen action, expecting that layer to be covered, would guard `semanticShowRect`; and on native Android the identifier is the resource-id, so a childless non-hittable full-screen ImageView or scrim with only a resource-id no longer paints, which means a stale earlier layer under it is no longer marked covered, so if real captures show that shape, would a typed hint from the Android helper (such as an opaque or clickable background) be better than inferring paint from the identifier?
